newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on export sales data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on export sales data.

text.p: Active exports and ideas that USDA Tuesday may make only a minimal hike in its estimate for 1996 U.S. soybean production, boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The export sales and weak doller plus ADM stopping the beans were the main things," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA Thursday said net export sales of U.S. soybeans during the week ended October 31 totaled 894,700 tonnes, above trade expectations for 750,000 tonnes, the traders said.
The market also was buoyed by a private estimate.
Sparks Companies Wednesday forecast 1996 U.S. soy output at 2.367 billion bushels below trade outlooks for 2.4 billion.

A Reuter survey of analysts indicated the crop at 2.376 billion bushels. The USDA November production report will be released Tuesday. Analysts said USDA would likely raise soybean production figures but year-end soybean stocks will remain tight. "You've got demand improving to the point that you've got to increase the crop or you have to lower the carry," said Steve Freed, analyst with ADM Investor Services.
Soybeans closed 3/4 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with November up 5-1/2 at $6.86-1/2.
The market also was supported by strong stopping of deliveries on the November for the second day in a row.
The ADM Investor Services house account Thursday stopped 2.2 million bushels of the 2.255 million posted Thursday for delivery on the November contract, according to the CBOT.
Traders said the soybean market was oversold and due for a bounce and the Refco Inc purchase of seven million bushels of January spurred an early rally.
Rain-delayed harvesting in the eastern U.S. growing region contributed to the advances, the traders said.
First resistance was noted in the November at $6.83-1/4 and second resistance at $6.89-1/2. The session high for November was $6.89.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts, up from 50,426 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, ADM Investor Services bought 400 January $7.50 calls at 3-1/4 and Refco Inc bought 500 January $6.25 puts at 2-1/8 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, up from 17,354 Wednesday.
